name: Monarchism in France
summary: French monarchism is the family of movements that want France to be a monarchy again, with a hereditary king (or, for Bonapartists, emperor) as head of state in place of the Republic. Its strands disagree on almost everything else: Legitimists back the senior Bourbons and a Catholic, counter-revolutionary kingship; Orleanists back the House of Orleans and historically a liberal constitutional monarchy; Bonapartists back an imperial, plebiscitary dynasty. What they share is the dynastic principle, a head of state above party politics who embodies national unity and continuity, and attachment to France's historic institutions.
scope: The profile represents what the main strands of French monarchism share today and at their peak: Legitimists (Chambord's 1871 manifesto, the modern Legitimist circles), Orleanists (the 1830 Charter, Action Francaise, the left-wing Nouvelle Action Royaliste) and, more loosely, Bonapartists. Positions on which they split, such as democracy, parliament, economics, immigration, minorities and the place of the Church, are recorded as 0 or low confidence. The distinctive far-right doctrine of Maurras and Action Francaise is not the profile's basis; it is covered by integral-nationalism, and the Legitimist and Bonapartist strands by legitimists and bonapartism.

keyFigures.name: Louis Philippe I
keyFigures.role: The Orleanist 'citizen king' of the July Monarchy (1830-1848)

keyFigures.name: Charles Maurras
keyFigures.role: Leader of Action Francaise, the most influential twentieth-century royalist movement

sources.title: Manifeste du comte de Chambord, 5 juillet 1871
sources.author: Henri, comte de Chambord (extract published by Dalloz Etudiant)
sources.usedFor: Legitimist programme: decentralisation and local liberties, the king's principle and flag, rejection of privileges and feudal rights, national unity, Alsace-Lorraine, order and liberty.

sources.title: Charte constitutionnelle du 14 aout 1830
sources.author: Wikisource (text of the Orleanist constitution)
sources.usedFor: Orleanist constitutional monarchy: equality before the law, consent of the chambers to taxes, religious and press freedom, property, the king's executive power and command of the forces, shared lawmaking, peers.

sources.title: Monarchism in France
sources.author: Wikipedia
sources.usedFor: The three strands, mostly constitutional aims, the Throne-and-Altar alliance, modern groups and their left-right placement, pretenders, the constitutional bar on changing the republican form.

sources.title: Orleanists
sources.author: Wikipedia
sources.usedFor: Orleanism as the liberal, pro-business centre; the 1830 Charter; the July Monarchy; Action Francaise's and NAR's variants.

sources.title: Legitimists
sources.author: Wikipedia
sources.usedFor: Counter-revolutionary views, Salic primogeniture and inalienable crown, Catholic king, Falloux law, Ultra-royalists, modern Legitimist organisations.

sources.title: Nouvelle Action Royaliste
sources.author: Wikipedia
sources.usedFor: The left-wing Orleanist strand: democratic constitutional monarchy, Gaullism, Keynesian economics, souverainism, anti-Atlanticism, support for immigrant voting rights.

sources.title: Action Francaise
sources.author: Wikipedia
sources.usedFor: The right-wing integral-royalist strand: anti-parliamentarism, federal monarchy, Catholicism as state religion, corporatism, nationalism, the 'four confederated states'.

sources.title: Bonapartism
sources.author: Wikipedia
sources.usedFor: The Bonapartist strand as restoration of the House of Bonaparte and its style of government; scholarly disagreement over its definition.

universal-healthcare.rationale: Royalists share no health policy: the Keynesian NAR would back public provision, while the pro-business Orleanist tradition leaned towards private means; inferred.

raise-minimum-wage.rationale: The strands split: NAR is Keynesian and anti-neoliberal, whereas Action Francaise wanted pay settled inside trade corporations rather than by statute.

markets-allocate-better.rationale: Classic Orleanism was a pro-business liberal platform, but Action Francaise rejected economic liberalism and NAR opposes neoliberalism, so royalists are divided.

public-ownership.rationale: Left-Gaullist NAR accepts a strong public sector, while the bourgeois Orleanist and right-wing groups do not; restoring a king implies no stance on it.

tax-the-wealthy.rationale: The 1830 Charter only asks each to pay in proportion to wealth; beyond that the left-wing NAR and right-wing groups would answer differently.

unions-good.rationale: The July Monarchy repressed strikes and Action Francaise preferred corporations to class unions, but NAR sits with the Gaullist left; split.

property-fundamental.rationale: The 1830 Charter declares all property inviolable and allows expropriation only for a lawful public interest with prior compensation; the right-wing strands share this, NAR less emphatically.

regulate-corporations.rationale: Orleanism was backed by financiers and business, whereas NAR is anti-neoliberal; no shared royalist view.

cut-welfare.rationale: Nothing common to the strands; NAR's Keynesianism opposes cuts while right-wing royalists have no settled doctrine on welfare.

worker-ownership.rationale: No strand proposes it: Action Francaise's corporatism keeps firms privately owned and Orleanism was a property-owning bourgeois platform.

surveillance-ok.rationale: Royalists promise order (Chambord pledged 'l'ordre et la liberte'), which suggests acceptance; inferred, and liberal royalists would be warier.

legalize-drugs.rationale: Inferred from the Catholic and traditionalist outlook of most royalists, tied to the Throne-and-Altar tradition.

restrict-hate-speech.rationale: NAR joined anti-racist campaigns with SOS Racisme, while Action Francaise's tradition is hostile to such laws; split.

strong-leader.rationale: Royalists want a king who can arbitrate above party conflict; NAR calls the Fifth Republic's strong presidency monarchical in inspiration and wants to extend it.

state-harmful.rationale: Every strand wants to restore a state with a king at its head; Chambord's manifesto offers to found with the French 'un gouvernement conforme aux besoins du pays'.

limit-guns.rationale: French royalist sources never treat gun ownership as an issue; no basis for either side.

empower-police-military.rationale: Order is a constant royalist theme and some monarchists joined the Resistance out of patriotism; inferred, not a stated programme.

legalize-sex-work.rationale: Inferred from the Catholic moral tradition most royalists share; the strands never addressed it.

decide-locally.rationale: Chambord's manifesto proposes to found the government on 'la decentralisation administrative et des franchises locales', and Action Francaise wanted a federal monarchy restoring provincial liberties; Orleanist and Bonapartist practice was more centralised.

rehabilitation.rationale: No royalist position on penal policy is documented across the strands.

traditional-family.rationale: Dynastic monarchy rests on family succession, and the Catholic Legitimist and Action Francaise strands make the family central; liberal Orleanists and NAR are less insistent.

same-sex-marriage.rationale: Inferred from the Catholic traditionalism of Legitimists and the right-wing groups; NAR may dissent.

abortion-legal.rationale: Inferred from the Catholic orientation of most royalist groups; the liberal and left strands could differ.

more-religion-public.rationale: The royalist cause is bound up with the alliance of Throne and Altar and Legitimists require a Catholic king, though the Orleanist Charter guarantees equal freedom for all faiths.

correct-racial-injustice.rationale: Most royalist groups sit on the right and would reject it, though the anti-racist NAR is an exception; inferred.

gender-social-construct.rationale: Inferred from the traditionalist Catholic outlook of most royalists.

preserve-national-culture.rationale: Royalists treat the dynasty as national heritage: Chambord refused to give up the flag of Henri IV and Joan of Arc 'avec lui que s'est faite l'unite nationale'.

gradual-change.rationale: Orleanists were the liberal centre of gradual constitutional change, but Legitimists were counter-revolutionaries and Action Francaise aimed at a coup.

reduce-immigration.rationale: Action Francaise's nationalism points one way, NAR's campaign for immigrant voting rights the other; restoring a king implies no immigration policy.

empower-international-orgs.rationale: Both the left-wing NAR (souverainist, anti-Atlanticist) and the nationalist right of Action Francaise defend national sovereignty against supranational bodies.

free-trade.rationale: NAR is anti-neoliberal and Action Francaise rejected economic liberalism; no strand today champions free trade, though early Orleanists were pro-business.

nation-first.rationale: Action Francaise's integral nationalism and NAR's souverainism both put national sovereignty first; liberal Orleanists were less doctrinaire.

humanitarian-intervention.rationale: No common royalist doctrine; NAR's anti-Atlanticism suggests scepticism, but the right has no settled view.

open-borders.rationale: Royalism is a national cause built on a dynasty that made French unity; even pro-immigrant NAR is souverainist rather than for open borders; inferred.

limit-growth.rationale: NAR has questioned growth models, but other strands have no position.

drastic-climate-action.rationale: Climate policy is not a royalist issue; the strands give no basis for a shared answer.

tech-solves-problems.rationale: Inferred from the traditionalist, Catholic temperament of most royalists, sceptical of faith in progress.

expand-nuclear.rationale: Inferred from souverainism and NAR's Gaullism, which valued national energy independence; never a royalist doctrine.

revolution-justified.rationale: Legitimists are defined by counter-revolution, yet the Orleanist monarchy came from the 1830 revolution and Action Francaise planned a coup; split.

experts-over-public.rationale: Action Francaise distrusted popular opinion while NAR defends representative democracy; no shared view.

central-planning.rationale: Orleanists were pro-business and Action Francaise favoured corporatism over state planning; even NAR is Keynesian, not planner.

socialized-markets.rationale: Royalist strands keep private property (protected in the 1830 Charter) and none calls for worker or public ownership of all firms.

land-value-tax.rationale: Tax design beyond the Charter's tax in proportion to wealth is not something any royalist strand has a view on, so no side can be inferred.

tax-inheritance.rationale: Inferred from the hereditary principle and the family's place in royalist thought; NAR's left economics might differ.

basic-income.rationale: Inferred: neither the corporatist nor the liberal royalist traditions support unconditional income.

tariffs-protect-industry.rationale: Souverainist royalists, NAR and Action Francaise alike, favour protecting national production; inferred.

state-directs-investment.rationale: Keynesian NAR would agree, while the pro-business Orleanist tradition would not.

widespread-small-property.rationale: Action Francaise's corporatist and Catholic-social milieu leaned this way; Orleanist business liberals did not.

abolish-money-wages.rationale: No strand, from liberal Orleanists to corporatists, envisages abolishing money; the Charter guarantees property.

abolish-central-banks.rationale: Inferred: royalists are statist rather than anarcho-capitalist, and NAR is Keynesian.

corporatist-bargaining.rationale: Action Francaise's corporatism supports it, but Orleanist liberalism and NAR's Keynesianism do not; split.

one-party-rule.rationale: Royalists want a king above parties, not a ruling party, and NAR backs representative democracy.

monarchy-legitimate.rationale: Restoring a monarchy is what defines the movement; Chambord's manifesto affirms 'mon principe' and asks France to call its king back.

democracy-best.rationale: Legitimists and Action Francaise opposed democracy, but NAR calls itself democratic; most royalists put the crown above elections.

direct-votes.rationale: The Orleanist Charter relies on elected chambers and Action Francaise distrusted popular votes; Bonapartist plebiscites are the exception.

workers-councils.rationale: No strand proposes councils; royalists base power on the crown with either chambers (Charter) or corporations (Action Francaise).

right-to-secede.rationale: Royalists celebrate the national unity the kings made (Chambord) even while backing provincial liberties; inferred.

natural-rulers.rationale: Hereditary monarchy assigns rule to one family by birth, which implies some are fitted to rule; liberal Orleanists and NAR would not frame it this way.

political-violence-never.rationale: Action Francaise had its street-fighting Camelots and coup plans, while NAR runs candidates in elections; split.

war-builds-character.rationale: No royalist doctrine on war's effect on national character.

separate-church-state.rationale: The Throne-and-Altar tradition, Legitimists' Catholic king and Action Francaise's call for Catholicism as state religion all reject strict separation; Orleanist pluralism softens it.

laws-from-scripture.rationale: Even Catholic royalists want law grounded in tradition and the Church, not scripture; the Charter is secular in its legal basis.

private-courts-defense.rationale: Justice and command of the forces belong to the crown (Charter arts. 12-13); privatising them is foreign to every strand.

military-superiority.rationale: Patriotic royalists support defence, but no strand seeks superiority over rivals; NAR is anti-Atlanticist rather than militarist.

ethnic-nation.rationale: Royalists see the nation as made by the dynasty and its history ('c'est avec lui que s'est faite l'unite nationale'), not by ethnicity; inferred.

class-struggle-history.rationale: Royalists credit dynasty, faith and national history, and Action Francaise opposed Marxism outright.

equal-outcomes.rationale: A hereditary monarchy accepts inherited rank; even the left-wing NAR seeks the common good rather than equal outcomes.

indigenous-land-authority.rationale: Not a royalist issue; no basis for a shared answer.

colonial-reparations.rationale: Inferred from royalist pride in France's historical record; not addressed.

civilizational-union.rationale: Souverainist royalists defend the French nation-state over wider unions.

self-interest-moral.rationale: Inferred from Catholic and corporatist ethics that put the common good above self-interest.

duties-before-rights.rationale: Catholic and Action Francaise royalists put duties first, though NAR defends the 1789 rights of man.

nature-intrinsic-value.rationale: Royalist texts are about the crown, the nation and religion; nothing in them bears on nature's intrinsic worth.

limit-population.rationale: Inferred from Catholic teaching and pro-family views.

industrial-civilization-disaster.rationale: No strand rejects industry; Orleanism was the party of financiers and business.

accelerate-technology.rationale: Inferred from the royalists' attachment to continuity and inherited institutions.

human-enhancement.rationale: Inferred from Catholic natural-law views common among royalists.

algorithmic-government.rationale: Inferred: royalists want personal, embodied authority in a king, not automated rule.

unbreakable-encryption.rationale: An anachronistic question for a movement whose doctrine was formed in the nineteenth century; its order-minded and liberal strands would pull opposite ways.

restore-past-order.rationale: Restoring the monarchy is by definition restoring a lost institution, and Legitimists are counter-revolutionary; but Orleanists and NAR want a modern monarchy compatible with 1789.

results-over-ideology.rationale: NAR's pragmatic Gaullism might agree; dynastic principle is itself ideological; no shared view.

direct-action.rationale: Action Francaise historically favoured street action and a coup, while NAR and today's royalist parties stand in elections.

means-match-ends.rationale: Royalists have disputed tactics (coup versus elections) but never framed the question this way, so there is no basis for a side.

return-to-foraging.rationale: Royalists aim to restore a historic state and its institutions; abandoning civilisation contradicts the whole project.

abolish-division-of-labor.rationale: Royalist thought is built on orders, trades and professions (Action Francaise's corporations), not their abolition.

distribute-by-need.rationale: No royalist strand is communist; the Charter protects property and Action Francaise opposed Marxism.

production-for-use.rationale: Royalists accept profit-making enterprise, whether liberal (Orleanist) or corporatist; inferred.

profit-exploitation.rationale: Action Francaise and Orleanists rejected Marxist analysis; NAR is Keynesian rather than Marxist.

dictatorship-of-proletariat.rationale: Royalists seek rule by a king above classes, the opposite of class dictatorship.

collective-farming.rationale: The Charter guarantees property and Legitimism's rural base was small and large landowners; no strand favours collectivisation.

capitalism-causes-war.rationale: Royalists blame republics and ideologies rather than capitalism for wars; inferred.

taxation-theft.rationale: The 1830 Charter requires every Frenchman to contribute to public expenses in proportion to his wealth; taxation is treated as a civic duty.

harm-principle.rationale: Catholic and traditionalist royalists accept moral legislation; liberal Orleanists less so.

individual-rights-only.rationale: Action Francaise stressed families, provinces and corporations, while NAR backs the 1789 rights of man; majority leans communitarian.

conscription.rationale: Inferred from royalist patriotism and service in war; not a documented doctrine.

exit-over-voice.rationale: Royalists see subjects bound by allegiance to the nation and its king, not as free to shop between states; inferred.

state-as-business.rationale: Royalists see the king as father and arbiter of the nation, not a manager of customers; inferred.

positive-liberty.rationale: NAR's social-democratic economics would agree, the liberal Orleanist tradition would not.

media-academia-power.rationale: Action Francaise denounced cultural elites, but this is not shared by the other strands.

hereditarian-race.rationale: Royalists define France by dynasty and history, and NAR is explicitly anti-racist; inferred.

organic-representation.rationale: Action Francaise and Legitimists wanted representation by families, provinces and trades, but the Orleanist Charter has elected deputies and NAR backs representative democracy.

total-state.rationale: Chambord promised decentralisation and local liberties, and the Charter guarantees religious and press freedom; no strand wants a total state.

national-rebirth.rationale: Royalists present the restoration as a remedy for the Republic's failings, Action Francaise most strongly; NAR is less apocalyptic.

territorial-expansion.rationale: Modern royalists have no expansionist programme; inferred.

personal-loyalty-rule.rationale: Chambord's manifesto dismisses talk of 'droits feodaux' as phantoms raised in bad faith; royalists want a national king, not feudal bonds.

bound-labor.rationale: Chambord explicitly rejected the return of tithes and feudal rights as phantoms; no strand wants serfdom.

no-neutral-knowledge.rationale: Inferred from Catholic and classical views of truth common among royalists.

universal-morality.rationale: Inferred from the Catholic natural-law tradition of most royalists; Maurras's positivism was an exception.

single-common-good.rationale: Royalists want a king above factions serving the common good; NAR's Renouvin frames monarchy as a means to the common good.

jewish-state-israel.rationale: French royalism has no doctrine on Zionism; Action Francaise's antisemitic past and NAR's positions give no shared answer.

diaspora-return-right.rationale: France has no diaspora-return question in royalist debate, so no side can be inferred.

revive-national-language.rationale: Not applicable: French has never fallen out of use.

workplace-democracy.rationale: Liberal and corporatist royalists keep management with owners; inferred.

school-vouchers.rationale: Catholic royalists defend church schools (the Falloux law), but a voucher system is not a stated position.

avoid-deficit-stimulus.rationale: Keynesian NAR rejects it, liberal Orleanists would accept it; split.

economic-freedom.rationale: Orleanist liberals tied political and economic liberty; Action Francaise did not.

rule-by-example.rationale: Royalists value the king's example but also law and charter; no settled view.

national-self-determination.rationale: Inferred from royalist souverainism and nationalism.

force-without-un.rationale: Inferred from souverainism and suspicion of international bodies.

reason-over-faith.rationale: Catholic royalists give faith a central place; inferred.

welfare-for-citizens.rationale: Right-wing royalists might agree, but NAR campaigned for immigrant rights; split.

work-for-welfare.rationale: No shared royalist position on welfare conditions.

class-collaboration.rationale: Action Francaise's corporatism unites employers and workers, and royalists see the king as above classes; NAR's Gaullism also favours cooperation.

sacrifice-heritage.rationale: Royalists treat inherited symbols and institutions as sacred trusts, as Chambord did with the white flag.

dominated-front.rationale: NAR is anti-Atlanticist but not aligned with the Global South; inferred.

workers-nation.rationale: Not a royalist issue except in Action Francaise's nationalism.

distinct-gender-roles.rationale: Legitimists keep Salic male succession to the throne, but no strand sets out wider legal gender roles.

ban-interest.rationale: Orleanism was backed by financiers; no strand proposes a ban.

racial-segregation-law.rationale: No royalist strand proposes racial segregation; NAR is explicitly anti-racist.

state-class-instrument.rationale: Royalists see the crown as above classes, the opposite of the Marxist view of the state.

expand-fossil-fuels.rationale: Energy production is not a royalist theme; only NAR's Gaullist interest in national independence touches it, without a stated view.

assimilate-immigrants.rationale: Nationalist royalists expect assimilation, but NAR's anti-racist stance differs; split.

elite-replacement.rationale: Some on the royalist far right hold such views, but NAR and Orleanist liberals reject them.

national-mission.rationale: No royalist doctrine of exporting a form of government.

patriarchy-structural.rationale: Inferred from traditionalist views common among royalists.

political-elite-corrupt.rationale: Action Francaise rallied opposition to a Republic it saw as corrupt, and royalists generally criticise the republican political class; NAR is milder.

heritable-defect-limits.rationale: Inferred from Catholic teaching against eugenics, which the Catholic majority of royalists follows.

security-forces-accountable.rationale: No royalist strand addresses accountability for past security-force abuses; left and right royalists would differ.

night-watchman-state.rationale: Royalists give the crown a broad role in national and social life; NAR is Keynesian; inferred.

discourage-race-mixing.rationale: Inferred: royalist nationhood is dynastic not racial, and NAR is anti-racist.

equal-moral-worth.rationale: The 1830 Charter opens 'Les Francais sont egaux devant la loi', Chambord disowned any return of privileges, and NAR upholds the 1789 Declaration.

settler-state-colonial.rationale: Royalist sources do not discuss settler states; no shared position can be drawn from them.

uniform-civil-code.rationale: Inferred from the Charter's equality before the law; French royalists do not propose religious civil codes.

restrict-conversion.rationale: The Charter guarantees equal freedom of worship; inferred for today.

ban-cattle-slaughter.rationale: A Hindu religious-law question with no counterpart in French Catholic royalism; inferred disagreement.

no-religion-state-schools.rationale: Legitimists backed the Falloux law restoring the Church's role in education; liberal strands differ.

state-strengthens-encirclement.rationale: A socialist doctrine royalists reject; inferred.

consent-of-governed.rationale: Louis-Philippe was made king by the chambers and NAR is democratic, but Legitimists base legitimacy on inherited right; split.

trade-surplus.rationale: Mercantilist trade targets are not discussed by royalists; souverainist leanings point slightly towards it but too weakly to choose.

population-transfer.rationale: Inferred; not a programme of any royalist strand.

initiating-force-wrong.rationale: Royalists want a state with armed forces and coercive law under the crown; libertarian non-aggression is foreign to them.

competition-drives-progress.rationale: Royalists prize order and cooperation; inferred.

ban-extremist-parties.rationale: Royalism itself seeks to end the republican form the constitution entrenches, so royalists reject outlawing parties for that aim; inferred.

freedom-as-non-domination.rationale: Royalists accept the king's reserve authority; inferred.

separated-powers.rationale: The Orleanist Charter divides executive power (the king) from lawmaking shared with two chambers, though Action Francaise wanted the king to reign and govern.

priority-to-poor.rationale: Not addressed beyond NAR's social economics.

right-to-buy-council-homes.rationale: Council-house sales are a British policy question no French royalist strand has addressed.

restrict-strikes-picketing.rationale: The July Monarchy repressed strikes, but NAR would oppose restrictions; split.

diversity-weakens-cohesion.rationale: Action Francaise would agree, NAR would not; split.

offices-by-lottery.rationale: Royalists favour heredity for the head of state and appointment by the crown; inferred.

emergency-suspend-protections.rationale: The Orleanist Charter forbids the king to suspend laws, while Action Francaise envisaged an authoritarian transition; split.

price-controls-essentials.rationale: Price policy is not discussed; corporatist and Keynesian royalists might accept it and liberal Orleanists not.

party-controls-media.rationale: The Charter declares that censorship can never be re-established, and royalists reject party rule; Action Francaise was less liberal.

party-commands-army.rationale: The Charter gives command of the armed forces to the king, not any party.

long-naturalization-wait.rationale: Naturalisation rules are not discussed; Action Francaise's nationalism and NAR's pro-immigrant stance would answer differently.

representatives-worker-pay.rationale: Royalists do not discuss deputies' pay; the question sits outside their focus on the head of state.

pool-sovereignty.rationale: NAR urged a no vote on the 2005 European Constitution and is souverainist; Action Francaise is nationalist.

head-commands-forces.rationale: The 1830 Charter states that executive power belongs to the king alone and that he commands the land and sea forces, declares war and makes treaties.

church-by-bishops.rationale: Catholic royalists accept episcopal church government; inferred.

clerical-rule.rationale: Royalists want a lay king allied with the Church, not rule by clergy.

defeat-own-government-war.rationale: Royalist patriotism runs the other way: some monarchists joined the Resistance out of patriotic concern.

censor-art-for-virtue.rationale: The Charter bans censorship, but the Catholic right is more willing; split.

unlimited-reelection.rationale: Royalists want a hereditary head, so presidential terms are secondary; NAR criticised the five-year term.

recall-officials.rationale: Inferred: royalists value stable authority over removable officials.

end-foreign-alliances.rationale: NAR's anti-Atlanticism points to leaving NATO, other strands differ.

abolish-rental-housing.rationale: Royalist respect for property implies owners may let; never addressed.

people-in-arms.rationale: The king commands regular forces under the Charter; inferred.

rural-life-healthier.rationale: Legitimism had a rural base, but this is not a doctrine of the family.

reunify-divided-nation.rationale: France is not a nation divided by an outside power, so royalism offers no position on this.

educated-out-of-touch.rationale: Royalist sources do not take a view on the educated classes as such; the movement's own leaders were largely intellectuals.

cultures-equal-different.rationale: Inferred from royalist pride in French civilisation.

death-penalty.rationale: The Ultra-royalists made sacrilege a capital crime, but modern left royalists would not back executions; split.

sex-ed-in-schools.rationale: Inferred from Catholic views of most royalists.

creationism-in-schools.rationale: Not addressed; French Catholicism does not generally push creationism.

restrict-pornography.rationale: Inferred from the Catholic moral outlook most royalists share; no strand states it.

citizenship-by-descent.rationale: Nationality law is not discussed; the nationalist right and the anti-racist NAR would answer differently.

minority-language-support.rationale: Inferred from royalist decentralism: Chambord's local liberties, Action Francaise's provinces and NAR's early regionalism.

religious-exemptions.rationale: The Charter gives every faith equal freedom and protection, but exemptions from general law are not discussed.

encourage-eccentricity.rationale: Inferred from traditionalist respect for custom.

sovereign-debt-cancellation.rationale: Third-world debt is not a royalist issue; NAR's left economics might favour relief, the right would not.

independence-needs-economic-change.rationale: A decolonisation question royalists do not address; no shared position follows from their principles.

constituent-assembly.rationale: A restoration needs constitutional change, and the royalist majority of 1871 was an elected assembly; but Legitimists hold the king's right does not come from an assembly.

restrict-freedoms-for-growth.rationale: Inferred from the Charter's guarantees; not addressed.

rich-countries-aid-poor.rationale: Development aid is not discussed; Catholic charity and souverainist priorities pull in different directions.

independent-nuclear-deterrent.rationale: Inferred from NAR's Gaullism and royalist souverainism.

direct-election-head-of-state.rationale: Royalists want a hereditary head of state; in Legitimist law the crown passes automatically to the heir on the king's death, leaving nothing to elect.

central-bank-independence.rationale: Not addressed; NAR's souverainism is sceptical.

no-land-for-peace.rationale: Not addressed beyond 1871 attachment to Alsace-Lorraine.

property-serves-common-good.rationale: The Charter treats property as inviolable, Catholic and corporatist royalists subordinate it to the common good; split.

soviet-state-capitalist.rationale: A Marxist debate about the Soviet Union in which royalists take no part.

precautionary-principle.rationale: Environmental risk policy is not discussed by any royalist strand.

collective-defense.rationale: NAR is anti-Atlanticist, other royalists do not address alliances.

annexed-territory-occupation.rationale: Chambord's 1871 manifesto honoured the 'fidelite' of annexed Alsace and Lorraine, implying the annexation was illegitimate; inferred for today.

subordinate-church-to-state.rationale: The Throne-and-Altar alliance and Legitimist Catholicism oppose curbing the Church; Orleanists were more Gallican.

nonpartisan-head-of-state.rationale: A hereditary king above party politics as a symbol of unity is the core case all strands make; NAR presents the monarch as embodying the common good.

force-to-prevent-secession.rationale: Inferred from royalist devotion to national unity.

region-keeps-system.rationale: Chambord's 'franchises locales' and Action Francaise's federal monarchy suggest openness to regional autonomy.

sacred-ruler.rationale: Legitimists keep the Catholic sacred kingship, but Orleanists and NAR see a constitutional monarch; split.

flat-income-tax.rationale: The Charter's tax in proportion to wealth predates income tax; no modern position.

character-from-environment.rationale: The nature-nurture question is not addressed; Catholic and positivist royalists would frame it differently.

sovereign-above-law.rationale: The Charter bars the king from suspending laws or dispensing from them, though the Ultra-royalists opposed limits on royal power.

space-expansion.rationale: Space policy is not a royalist concern and nothing in the strands' principles settles it.

mixed-constitution.rationale: The Charter combines a king, appointed (possibly hereditary) peers and elected deputies; Action Francaise would put more weight on the king.

leader-cult.rationale: Royalists honour the dynasty, but mass praise is not part of the tradition; split.

equal-parenting.rationale: Custody law is not discussed; Catholic family views do not settle this statement either way.

land-redistribution.rationale: The Charter protects property, including land sold off in the Revolution, against seizure.

refugee-return.rationale: Refugee return is not a question royalists address.

co-ethnic-territorial-claim.rationale: Royalists define France by dynasty and history rather than ethnicity, but claims on co-nationals abroad are not discussed.

apostasy-punishable.rationale: The Charter states that each professes his religion with equal freedom; no modern royalist group seeks penalties.

women-must-cover.rationale: Mandatory veiling has no basis in French Catholic royalism or its liberal strands; inferred.

common-currency.rationale: Inferred from royalist souverainism and opposition to European integration.

kin-peoples-union.rationale: Royalists defend the existing French nation-state; inferred.

national-cultural-autonomy.rationale: Minority cultural institutions are not discussed directly; decentralism favours them while the national-unity theme does not.

rights-where-you-live.rationale: A question from Jewish political debate that royalists do not address.

material-conditions-drive-history.rationale: Royalists explain history by dynasty, faith and national tradition; inferred.

ban-cartels.rationale: Competition policy is not discussed; Orleanist business ties and NAR's anti-neoliberalism point opposite ways.

no-bailouts.rationale: Bank bailouts are not discussed; Keynesian NAR and liberal royalists would differ.

gender-parity-bodies.rationale: Inferred from traditionalist views of most royalists.

economic-self-sufficiency.rationale: No colonial bloc in modern royalism; inferred.

trade-labor-env-standards.rationale: Trade agreement design is not discussed by royalists.

moral-incentives.rationale: Socialist work incentives are outside royalist debate; Catholic duty and private enterprise pull different ways.

armed-group-creates-revolution.rationale: Royalists reject revolutionary vanguards; Action Francaise's coup plans were a restoration, not revolution.

abolish-hereditary-privilege.rationale: Royalists defend a hereditary crown and the Charter allowed hereditary peerages, but Chambord disowned any return of 'privileges'.

history-own-civilization.rationale: Inferred from royalist devotion to national history and its kings.

civilizing-tutelage.rationale: Colonial tutelage is not discussed in the sources on today's royalism; past imperial attitudes are not a shared doctrine.

patriotic-education.rationale: Inferred from royalist patriotism and devotion to national symbols, like Chambord's flag.

end-racial-preferences.rationale: France has no racial preferences in admissions or hiring, so the question does not arise in royalist debate.

public-money-creation.rationale: Monetary design is not a stated royalist theme; souverainists favour national monetary control without saying this.

capitalism-adapts.rationale: A forecast about capitalism that no royalist strand makes; their critiques of liberalism concern its morals, not its collapse.

former-empire-influence.rationale: Royalists do not discuss France's former colonies as a sphere of influence.

delink-world-market.rationale: A dependency-theory prescription royalists do not discuss; NAR's souverainism stops short of it.

freedom-to-discriminate.rationale: Anti-discrimination law is not discussed; liberal and anti-racist royalists would differ from the nationalist right.

entrenched-bill-of-rights.rationale: The Orleanist Charter and NAR's support for the 1789 Declaration favour written rights, Action Francaise did not; split.

colonial-treaties-void.rationale: Colonial treaties are not discussed by any royalist strand.

elective-rulers.rationale: Legitimists hold the crown inalienable and passed by Salic primogeniture, and Chambord claimed the throne by his 'principe'; royalists reject choosing the ruler by election.

minority-veto.rationale: Royalists accept binding laws made by king and chambers; inferred.

resist-lawless-ruler.rationale: Orleanists came to power in 1830 by removing Charles X for breaking the Charter, while Legitimists reject that right; split.

parliament-supreme.rationale: The Charter shares lawmaking between the king and two chambers, and Action Francaise was anti-parliamentary; no strand makes parliament supreme.

animal-suffering-matters.rationale: Animal ethics is outside royalist doctrine.

animal-use-humane.rationale: Animal welfare in farming and research is not discussed by royalists.

noblesse-oblige.rationale: Inferred from Catholic social thought and aristocratic tradition.

mass-culture-pacifies.rationale: A critical-theory claim royalists do not make; Action Francaise blamed democracy, not mass culture, for decline.

ruling-class-consent.rationale: A Gramscian claim that royalists neither adopt nor discuss.

world-economy-extracts-surplus.rationale: Dependency theory is not part of royalist thought; the right-wing strands reject Marxist economics; inferred.

native-born-offices.rationale: Eligibility for office apart from the throne is not discussed; strands would differ.

party-own-road.rationale: A question internal to communist parties, which royalists reject altogether.

self-reliance-over-aid.rationale: Development strategy for poor countries is not discussed by royalists.

return-lost-territory.rationale: Chambord's 1871 manifesto invoked lost Alsace and Lorraine; no modern claims.

indigenous-political-leadership.rationale: Rule by pre-colonial peoples' descendants has no place in royalist thought, which centres on a dynasty; inferred.

antifascism-founding-value.rationale: Some monarchists joined the Resistance while Action Francaise welcomed Vichy; split.

totalitarianisms-equivalent.rationale: Royalists are divided by their Second World War history (Resistance versus Vichy), and none states this equivalence.

slavery-not-civil-war-cause.rationale: An American historical question outside French royalist debate.

preserve-contested-monuments.rationale: Inferred from royalist attachment to national memory and its symbols.

male-disadvantage-attention.rationale: Gender policy for men is not discussed by royalists.

domestic-violence-symmetry.rationale: Domestic violence services are not discussed by royalists.

institutions-fit-civilization.rationale: Royalists hold that France's own historic monarchy suits it better than imported forms; inferred.

military-guardian-role.rationale: Royalists give the armed forces to the king, not a political role of their own; not addressed.

paid-care-work.rationale: Paying domestic work is not discussed; Catholic family values do not settle it.

filial-duty.rationale: Inferred from Catholic family ethics and the dynastic respect for inheritance shared by most royalists.

office-by-exam.rationale: Recruitment to administrative posts is not discussed in the royalist sources.

foreign-takeover-block.rationale: Inferred from the souverainism of NAR and the nationalist right, which favour national control of strategic firms.

no-fault-divorce.rationale: Inferred from the Catholic view of marriage held by most royalists; liberal strands might differ.

individual-pension-accounts.rationale: Pension design is not discussed; NAR's Keynesianism would oppose it and liberal royalists might not.

land-use-tenure.rationale: The Charter makes property inviolable; inferred.

budget-needs-parliament.rationale: The 1830 Charter provides that no tax may be levied unless both chambers consent; Action Francaise gave assemblies less weight.

single-official-language.rationale: Decentralist royalists favour regional languages, but French is the national language; split.

foreign-land-ownership.rationale: Foreign land ownership is not discussed by royalists.

disparate-impact-discrimination.rationale: Inferred from the right-wing majority of royalists; NAR's anti-racism might lead it elsewhere.

consumerism-harmful.rationale: NAR questions growth models; others do not address it.

arm-foreign-insurgents.rationale: Covert foreign policy is not discussed by royalists.

intervene-in-bloc.rationale: Souverainist royalists oppose interference in sovereign states; inferred.

corporate-influence.rationale: Orleanists were backed by financiers, while NAR is anti-neoliberal; split.

restrict-foreign-funding.rationale: Inferred from royalist souverainism, which puts national independence first.

residents-only-property.rationale: Local housing rules are not discussed by royalists.

job-guarantee.rationale: Keynesian NAR might support it, others not; split.

democratic-peace.rationale: Royalists do not share faith in spreading democracy; inferred.

industrial-unions.rationale: Union structure is not a royalist question; Action Francaise preferred trade corporations to either form.

minority-conspiracy.rationale: Action Francaise denounced the 'four confederated states' of Jews, Protestants, Freemasons and foreigners, but Orleanist liberals and the anti-racist NAR reject such views.

abolish-legal-marriage.rationale: Inferred from the Catholic family views of most royalists, for whom marriage is a public institution.

public-access-to-information.rationale: Freedom of information law is not discussed by royalists.

local-production.rationale: Local production is not a stated royalist theme despite their decentralism.

informal-organisation.rationale: Royalists organise in standing associations and parties such as NAR and the Legitimist circles.

national-law-over-international.rationale: Souverainism is shared by NAR and the nationalist right of Action Francaise.

religious-nation.rationale: Legitimists require a Catholic king, but the Orleanist Charter grants equal religious freedom and NAR is secular-democratic; split.

deference-to-leading-power.rationale: Royalist souverainism rejects deference to any power; inferred.

personal-possessions-private.rationale: The Charter protects all property, means of production included; royalists reject common ownership.

defeat-communism.rationale: Action Francaise opposed Marxism; NAR is not anti-communist in this sense.

mixed-public-service-providers.rationale: Public service delivery is not discussed; NAR and liberal royalists would differ.

religion-illusion.rationale: Royalism is bound to the Throne-and-Altar tradition and Legitimists require a Catholic king; Maurras's agnosticism was an exception.

capitalism-progressive.rationale: Orleanists embraced commerce, Action Francaise rejected liberal capitalism; split.

women-equality-needs-economic-change.rationale: Inferred: royalists do not tie women's position to transforming the economic system, which most strands defend.

socialized-care.rationale: Inferred from the royalist view of the family as the basic unit of society that raises its own children.

purge-loanwords.rationale: Language purism is not a stated royalist cause.

treaties-binding.rationale: Treaties with internal nations are not a French royalist question.

cooperative-communities.rationale: Inferred from royalists' defence of private property and national institutions.

majority-settlement.rationale: Inferred; settlement policy is not discussed and royalism defines the nation dynastically rather than ethnically.

neither-capitalism-nor-communism.rationale: Action Francaise sought a corporatist third way, but Orleanists were pro-business liberals; split.

historical-land-claim.rationale: Chambord's manifesto addresses Alsace-Lorraine, but strands differ and no shared line on historic claims exists.

holocaust-denial.rationale: Not discussed in the sources; no strand holds it, so rejection is inferred.

criminalize-homosexuality.rationale: Legitimists, rooted in Catholic tradition, would lean to yes while Orleanists and the left-wing NAR would not; the strands split.

suppress-opposition.rationale: The Orleanist Charter guaranteed press freedom and assembly of the chambers, but Action Francaise was anti-parliamentarian; inferred as mostly opposed.

punish-blasphemy.rationale: Legitimists and Action Francaise favour a Catholic state religion while Orleanists and NAR do not.

colonies-serve-metropole.rationale: Not a shared issue; Bonapartists were imperial while the Charter and NAR are silent on colonies.

defensive-jihad-duty.rationale: The strands share no view; the sources do not address jihad.

unreligious-rulers-fought.rationale: Orleanists and NAR accept constitutional rule, while Legitimists defended the crown and altar; inferred as mostly opposed to forcible removal.

participatory-democracy.rationale: NAR is democratic but Action Francaise and Legitimists are anti-parliamentarian; the strands split.

intersecting-oppressions.rationale: The strands share no analysis of overlapping oppression, and the dynastic principle stresses national unity; inferred.

gender-identity-recognition.rationale: Not addressed; the Legitimist and Catholic strands oppose it while others are silent, inferred.

assisted-dying.rationale: Not addressed; Catholic and traditionalist strands would oppose it while NAR may differ, inferred.

left-right-obsolete.rationale: A head of state above party appeals across left and right, but adherents themselves place strands on both sides.

alienated-labor.rationale: The strands do not use a Marxist analysis; Action Francaise favoured corporatism over class struggle, inferred.

islam-incompatible.rationale: Strands split: Legitimists and Action Francaise are suspicious of Islam while NAR backed immigrant voting rights.

divine-source-of-authority.rationale: Legitimists hold a Catholic kingship by divine right while Orleanists rest on the 1830 Charter and the chambers.

religious-dress-in-state.rationale: French laicite is a republican norm and the strands split on the Church's place in the state.

ban-nda-harassment.rationale: Not addressed by the sources; strands have no shared line.

social-market-economy.rationale: Orleanism is pro-business and liberal while NAR is Keynesian and Action Francaise corporatist; the strands split.

abolish-armed-forces.rationale: The Charter gives the king command of the forces, and the strands treat the crown as embodying national continuity and defence.

rich-first.rationale: Not addressed by the sources; strands have no shared line.

stay-neutral-between-blocs.rationale: NAR was anti-Atlanticist and Gaullist while other strands had no line on blocs; the strands split.

dynastic-succession.rationale: The dynastic principle is what defines the strands: Legitimists hold Salic primogeniture and an inalienable crown, Orleanists and Bonapartists hold hereditary dynasties.

interest-free-mutual-credit.rationale: Royalist strands do not discuss mutual credit; Action Francaise's corporatism and the Orleanist pro-business tradition both point away from it; inferred.

refuse-lender-austerity.rationale: The strands split: the sovereigntist, anti-Atlanticist NAR would refuse, whereas the pro-business Orleanist tradition accepts lender terms.

property-franchise.rationale: Historic Orleanism used a tax-based franchise under the 1830 Charter, while the modern NAR favours democratic suffrage, so the strands split.

domination-women-nature.rationale: Royalism has no shared position on ecofeminism; Legitimist traditionalists reject it and the left-leaning NAR may sympathise; inferred.

reification.rationale: Strands outside the NAR defend property and markets and would not adopt a critique of capitalism; inferred.

press-owned-by-wealth.rationale: Orleanists defended press freedom in the Charter while the NAR criticises money power; Action Francaise had its own press; adherents split.

promulgated-standing-laws.rationale: The 1830 Charter set equality before the law and the king's role under fixed law, and Chambord's manifesto speaks of order and liberty; Bonapartist plebiscitary rule is a partial exception.

racial-franchise.rationale: The Charter's equality before the law and the NAR's support for immigrant voting rights point against racial limits, though Action Francaise's nationalism is more exclusionary.

online-participation.rationale: Royalist strands do not address online participation, and their views of direct versus representative democracy differ; inferred.

open-government-data.rationale: No shared position: the NAR and Orleanist liberals favour openness, while Action Francaise and Bonapartism favoured strong executive discretion; inferred.

interfaith-marriage-restriction.rationale: The Charter guaranteed religious freedom, though Legitimists want a Catholic kingship; strands differ, with a modern majority against legal limits; inferred.

boycott-minority-shops.rationale: Action Francaise had antisemitic currents, but modern royalist movements mostly do not endorse boycotts of religious minorities; inferred.

citizens-assembly.rationale: Inferred from the shared dynastic principle of a hereditary head of state embodying continuity over popular mechanisms; the strands split on democracy and none of the sources mention lot-selected assemblies.

reinterpret-religion.rationale: Inferred from the Legitimist attachment to a Catholic, counter-revolutionary kingship and historic institutions; Orleanists and the left-wing Nouvelle Action Royaliste differ, so confidence is low.

wealth-concentration-endangers-liberty.rationale: Strands split: Legitimists and the left-wing Nouvelle Action Royaliste worry about money power, Orleanist bourgeois liberals do not; inferred from the strands' differing economics.

open-lgbt-military-service.rationale: Adherents are split: Legitimist Catholics oppose it while Orleanist and Bonapartist strands are indifferent; inferred from the strands' differing attitudes to the Church and social change.

state-promotes-atheism.rationale: Every strand rejects state atheism: Legitimists defend Catholic kingship and the others accept the Church's place in French history, as the Chambord manifesto and Charter's religious clauses show.

abolish-police-prisons.rationale: Monarchists defend the state's authority and historic institutions, so abolishing police and prisons is inconsistent with all strands; inferred from their order-and-continuity emphasis.

power-sharing-divided-societies.rationale: The movement never addressed consociationalism; the king as unifying head above communities points mildly one way but strands disagree on parliament, so inferred as split.

charity-over-state-aid.rationale: Legitimist subsidiarity and Catholic social tradition favour local communities and charity over centralised state programmes, while Bonapartists were more statist; inferred from the Legitimist outlook.

term-limits.rationale: A hereditary monarch has no term, and the strands favour continuity of office over rotation; inferred from the dynastic principle, not stated for legislators.

vote-delegation.rationale: Delegable direct democracy is far from the dynastic, institution-bound outlook of the strands, though Bonapartist plebiscites show some taste for direct appeals; inferred.

existential-risk-priority.rationale: Never addressed; the strands neither prioritise nor oppose it, so inferred as indifferent.

women-in-religious-leadership.rationale: Legitimist Catholic tradition reserves priesthood to men, and the other strands do not push for change; inferred from the Church's position that Legitimists defend.

shared-marital-authority.rationale: The Napoleonic Code placed wives under husbands' authority and Legitimists defend traditional family order; modern royalists vary, so a low-confidence inference.

foreign-residents-local-vote.rationale: Inferred: the strands tie political membership to the French nation and its institutions, and do not take up non-citizen voting.

rent-control.rationale: Strands split on economic intervention, so rent control is left unsettled; inferred.

abolish-ip.rationale: Inferred from the 1830 Charter's protection of property and the tradition's conservative view of property; the sources do not discuss intellectual property.

uniformed-youth.rationale: Inferred: Action Francaise had its own youth groups, but the profile's broader monarchism does not call for drilled national-service youth movements.

no-nuclear-weapons-on-territory.rationale: Inferred: the strands generally support France's own national defence and deterrent, so the question of hosting nuclear weapons is not their concern.

no-foreign-bases.rationale: Inferred: the royalist emphasis on national independence and the left-wing Nouvelle Action Royaliste's opposition to alignment favour no foreign bases.

recognise-genocide.rationale: Strands split and the sources do not address formal genocide recognition; inferred.

income-for-work-not-ownership.rationale: Strands split on economics, from Orleanist liberals to the social monarchism of Nouvelle Action Royaliste; inferred.

never-kill-self-defence.rationale: Inferred from the Catholic doctrine of Legitimists and the conservative strands, which allow defensive killing in just defence.

unbroken-national-continuity.rationale: The dynastic principle, which Chambord's manifesto affirms, rests on continuity from France's historic kingdom to the present.

sex-socially-constructed.rationale: Inferred from the Catholic and traditional-family outlook of the main strands; not addressed in the sources.

no-fixed-category-of-women.rationale: Inferred from the traditional views of the Legitimist and conservative strands, though Nouvelle Action Royaliste differs.

martyrs-honoured.rationale: Inferred: Legitimists venerate Louis XVI and the victims of the Revolution as martyrs, but other strands do not.

politics-spiritual-struggle.rationale: Legitimists read politics as a Catholic counter-revolutionary struggle, while Orleanists and Bonapartists do not; the strands split.

homeland-cultural-centre.rationale: Inferred: the profile's monarchism is tied to the French state and its institutions, not a homeland serving a diaspora.

culture-before-state.rationale: Action Francaise's 'politique d'abord' put restoring the monarchy before cultural renewal, and the dynastic strands share that priority; inferred.

god-not-male.rationale: Inferred from the traditional Catholic outlook of the main strands; not addressed in the sources.

scripture-judged-by-women.rationale: Inferred from the traditional Catholic outlook of the main strands; not addressed in the sources.

economy-in-majority-hands.rationale: Action Francaise was hostile to minorities in economic life, but Orleanists and Bonapartists were not, so the strands split.

single-unit-for-people.rationale: Anachronistic; nothing in the sources links monarchism to merging regions by people, and the tradition defends France's historic provinces and unity.

notes: Strands split on most questions outside the monarchy itself. Action Francaise (and the older Legitimists) answer the far-right and Catholic-integralist way on democracy, parliament, minorities and the Church; Nouvelle Action Royaliste is democratic, Keynesian and anti-racist; classic Orleanists were liberal and pro-business; Bonapartists add plebiscites and a centralised state. The previous version of this audit followed Maurras alone and duplicated integral-nationalism; its candidate statement on the French Revolution (merged as restore-past-order) is an Action Francaise and Legitimist position that NAR, which accepts 1789, does not share.
